GC races normal reservation publication: publish_exclusive can unlink a temporary file after glob() returns it but before stat(), causing an uncaught FileNotFoundError that aborts the entire sweep. Concurrent GC processes similarly race the unlinks; disappearing per-path entries must be treated as benign.

transfer_holder authorizes ownership transfer solely by matching the publicly readable current lane_id; it never accepts or verifies the dead-claim liveness evidence required for the named D2 exception. Any caller can therefore seize a live open reservation and subsequently pass the holder-only transition checks. After a CAS loss, update_payload unconditionally reapplies the original values to the re-read head without validating that they are still current. A delayed PR-creation backfill can therefore overwrite a newer final-gate head_sha/base_sha while retaining that newer generation's attested_merge_tree, producing an inconsistent merge-door tuple. The CAS test covers only conflicting state transitions and stays green for this payload race.

The durable payload boundary validates field names but never their declared types or value domains. The CLI/Python API can persist values such as pr={}, head_sha=[], or concurrent_lanes_min=-1, despite the reservation contract requiring int/null, SHA/null, and nonnegative lane counts; downstream merge-door consumers will then crash or leave the arc blocked.

arc_id validation permits dot-prefixed identifiers, including the reserved value .seq. Such a reservation shares the sequence allocator directory and is then skipped by sibling_open_count and gc because both ignore dot-prefixed directories, making a validly created reservation invisible to coordination and retention logic.

round_outcomes is keyed only by round_n, but the existing wrappers allocate round numbers independently per producer. A Codex-unavailable to Gemini failover can therefore record both channels as round 1, and the second CAS overwrites the first, erasing REVIEWER_UNAVAILABLE and corrupting the durable audit and N6 exclusion. The test avoids this by using rounds 1 and 2.

GC skips the temporary-file sweep whenever a reservation directory has no JSON head. A crash during first-generation publication leaves exactly such a directory containing only .1.json.<pid>.tmp, so this required orphan cleanup can never remove it; the test creates a successful reservation before its tmp file and misses this crash state.

superseded_by is applied on every legal transition when supplied, so open->merged can create a merged reservation carrying a supersession pointer. This contradicts the three-state record semantics, where superseded_by belongs to abandoned records, and leaves authoritative state with mutually inconsistent landing metadata.

TRANSITION_MUTABLE permits concurrent_lanes_at_open on every transition, not only pending->open. A holder can therefore overwrite the cohort sensor during open->merged or open->abandoned, corrupting the value that is contractually captured at the pending->open flip; the tests exercise only the valid edge.

record_phase performs no state check, and record_round_outcome has the same omission. A late phase emitter or review-wrapper process can therefore publish new generations after the reservation is merged or abandoned, making terminal audit and measurement data race with post-merge activity instead of being confined to the active arc window.

round_outcomes is keyed only by round_n, but existing review emitters allocate rounds per producer. In the normal Codex-unavailable to Gemini-failover path, both channels can emit round 1; this conflict raises and is caught by record_round_outcome_if_reserved, leaving only REVIEWER_UNAVAILABLE instead of the failover verdict. Allocate rounds globally or include channel/producer in the key.

update_payload replays updates against any re-read head without rejecting terminal states. If its CAS loses to open-to-merged, it can apply stale or cleared head_sha/base_sha/attested_merge_tree values onto a new merged generation, corrupting the terminal audit used by later attestation and first-parent checks. Refuse payload updates on merged or abandoned heads.

Every RoundOutcomeConflict is treated as a cross-channel collision and re-recorded under the next free integer. After codex round 1 and gemini round 1, gemini's actual round 1 is stored as key 2; a later codex round 2 then moves to key 3. The map keys therefore stop representing round_n, breaking the per-round audit contract and joins to the gate log. Same-channel conflicts are also silently renumbered instead of reported. Use an arc-wide round identity or preserve producer plus round explicitly.

The abandoned transition checks only that superseded_by is truthy. A nonexistent or invalid target such as '../missing' is therefore committed into an immutable terminal head; walk_terminal subsequently raises, and no legal transition can repair the reservation. Validate the target as an arc_id and require its reservation to exist before terminalizing.

reserve() persists caller-supplied arc_type_declared_at without validating it. Although reservation creation is the required open-time capture point, callers can store 'close' or an arbitrary value, causing downstream folding to omit arc_type_open and permanently contaminating cohort data. Require the value to be 'open' or remove the parameter.

The supplied round_n is discarded and every call allocates a new key. This breaks the C-HE-25 {round_n: outcome} contract and the explicit writer's idempotency: retrying the same arc/round creates a duplicate outcome, while non-colliding rounds can be renumbered so the folded reservation no longer joins to the gate-log round. Preserve round_n and allocate a fallback key only after detecting a genuine cross-channel collision.

gc() accepts symlinked entries because Path.is_dir() follows symlinks, then current() and d.glob('*.json') traverse the target and unlink numeric JSON files below a forged terminal head. A symlink placed under the shared writable reservations root can therefore make GC delete files outside QUEUE_DIR; reject symlinks and enforce the resolved-path boundary before reading or pruning.

The holder check applies only to open reservations, so any lane can perform pending->abandoned by naming any existing superseder. The public transition CLI supplies neither operator RESOLVED-HIL evidence nor proof that the caller owns the superseding reservation, allowing a competing lane to terminalize another lane's selected unit and remove its scheduling fence.

Normal reservation writes follow a pre-created symlink at reservations/<arc_id>: mkdir(exist_ok=True) accepts a symlink to a directory and publish_exclusive then creates generation files in its external target. current() likewise trusts that target. The diff guards symlinks only in gc(), leaving state reads forgeable and writes able to escape QUEUE_DIR.

On a cross-channel collision, the wrapper persists the outcome under a newly invented arc-level round number. For example, Gemini round 1 becomes reservation key 2 while its gate-log row remains round 1. Because C-HE-25 defines the map as keyed by round_n, the folded arc record no longer joins to the actual review and falsely reports a round that never occurred.

record_round_outcome_next is not idempotent across CAS retries. If two processes persist the same failover outcome concurrently, both initially choose key 2; after one wins, the loser re-runs build, chooses key 3, and stores a duplicate outcome, inflating the durable round history. The sequential tests do not exercise this race.

finding_count is coerced with int() but never checked for a nonnegative integer, so API calls and the CLI can persist values such as -1 (and API booleans become 0/1). This corrupts the measurement field used by later review analytics; validate the count at the write funnel.

The collision fallback makes a later legitimate same-channel round unrecordable. After Codex round 1 occupies key 1, Gemini failover round 1 is moved to key 2; Gemini's next producer round is 2, so it collides with key 2, this branch classifies it as an anomaly, and the outer handler only logs the loss. Use a stable composite identity or retain the producer round separately.

Idempotency is inferred by comparing the row payload against every historical round. Distinct rounds commonly have identical channel/terminal/finding_count values, so a later round routed through this fallback can return unchanged merely because an earlier round had the same outcome, silently deleting per-round audit and N6 data. Deduplication needs an invocation or source-round identity.

The superseder-holder check applies to open->abandoned as well as pending->abandoned. If lane A holds the old open arc and lane B holds its confirmed superseding reservation, lane A cannot terminalize its own CLOSED arc even though the contract requires only the open holder plus the confirmed pointer; the old reservation is stranded. Scope this ownership check to pending abandonment.

The symlink defense is TOCTOU: _dir() checks is_symlink(), returns, and _write_gen() subsequently calls mkdir(exist_ok=True) and publishes through that path. A concurrent process can install a symlink between those operations; mkdir accepts a link to a directory and the generation is written outside QUEUE_DIR. The added test covers only a pre-planted symlink.

The authority-bearing lane_id validator permits both None and the empty string. reserve(), pending->open, and transfer_holder() can therefore create an open reservation with no distinguishable holder; the holder CLI reports the same empty output as no holder and future holder-gated append cannot authorize the lane. Require a nonempty valid lane identifier.

Outcomes are keyed as <round>/<channel>, but C-HE-25 requires {round_n: {...}} and the planned U-HE-19 fold directly copies this map. Failover creates both 1/codex and 1/gemini, which cannot be projected to one round 1 entry without dropping or renumbering a leg; the eventual arc row must therefore violate the contract or lose audit data.

The .seq directory lacks the symlink and containment checks applied to arc directories. mkdir(exist_ok=True) accepts a symlink to a directory, so a pre-planted reservations/.seq link makes alloc_seq enumerate and create numeric files outside QUEUE_DIR, violating store containment and allowing external contents to control the ordering authority.

current() accepts any numeric *.json entry and read_text() follows file symlinks. A pre-planted reservations/<arc>/999.json symlink can therefore inject a forged head from outside QUEUE_DIR, and subsequent CAS operations treat that payload as authoritative; the existing test covers only a symlinked arc directory.

The containment boundary is derived from reservations_root().resolve() without rejecting reservations_root() itself when it is a symlink. A pre-planted QUEUE_DIR/reservations symlink therefore makes the checks pass relative to the external target; writers create state there, and gc() can traverse and unlink matching generation files outside QUEUE_DIR.

_check_id explicitly permits None even though every caller uses it for a required lane authority. reserve(), pending->open transition(), and transfer_holder() can consequently persist lane_id=null; holder() then reports no holder, and the holder equality check can be satisfied by another lane_id=None call, defeating the intended holder fence.

The declared <sha|null>/<oid|null> fields are validated only as arbitrary strings. The composite `<round>/<channel>` keys drift from C-HE-25 and ArcRow's committed `{round_n: outcome}` contract. Reservation arc-id validation is weaker than the closure queue's validation: values containing `.taken` or exceeding the recovery-suffix byte budget can be reserved successfully but are later rejected by `queue_capture`. Caller-supplied phase timestamps are persisted without validating the required ISO-8601 UTC format. A truthy value such as `t0` becomes part of an immutable snapshot and later duration consumers cannot parse it, poisoning the C-HE-27 measurement record.

Composite keys such as "1/codex" are incompatible with C-HE-25 and the committed U-HE-19 consumer, which folds round_outcomes verbatim and asserts a "1" key. record_phase silently overwrites an existing phase edge. The terminal transition is not bound to the PR whose ground truth was checked. At this HEAD, tools/hooks/loop_lib.sh does not define loop_log_structured, so the real emit_loop_row raises on this first NOTIFY and the following durable DEFERRED-HIL row is never attempted. reconcile_all only returns an ephemeral ERROR value, violating the C-HE-20 durable-HITL contract; the tests hide this by monkeypatching emit_loop_row.

The per-arc current() read occurs outside the isolation try block. A single symlinked generation, malformed JSON snapshot, or other ReservationError here aborts the entire pass before later arcs are reconciled, contradicting reconcile_all's stated fault-isolation contract. Concurrent reconcile passes are not idempotent: both can observe open/MERGED, the first writes merged, and the second replays transition against the terminal head and raises IllegalTransition, producing an ERROR/exit 2 despite the desired state already being reached. The idempotency test is sequential and does not exercise this normal multi-session race.

The shell redirection opens and truncates .reconcile.log before reservations.py can perform its symlink checks. Because the preceding -d test follows symlinks, a symlinked reservations directory or .reconcile.log can cause every SessionStart to truncate an arbitrary writable file. Refuse symlinks and open the output through a containment-checked mechanism.

This enables reconciliation before its declared U-HE-29 dependency exists: loop_lib.sh has no loop_log_structured, so every aged/stuck reservation makes emit_loop_row fail. reconcile-all converts that failure to exit 2, but the detached hook ignores the exit and writes only to a truncated log that loop_pending_hil_summary never reads. Per-arc corruption isolation is incomplete. current() performs no schema validation, so a valid JSON head such as {} raises KeyError here and a non-object head raises TypeError; neither is caught by the ReservationError/OSError/ValueError handler. One malformed reservation therefore aborts reconcile-all and prevents later arcs from being reconciled.

The manifest-covered TTL test replaces emit_loop_row with a no-op and checks only the return value and unchanged state. The new durable `.reconcile.log` store is absent from the C-HE-30 store audit. The existing `test_store_audit.py::test_every_path_literal_in_modules_is_listed` deterministically fails with `tools/reservations.py: store literal '.reconcile.log' not in audit`, so the committed phase-0 gate is red.

The detached reconciliation discards stdout, stderr, and its exit status. If `_write_store_log` fails (including the explicitly tested planted-symlink case), no new log exists and no additionalContext reports the failure, turning the claimed loud/nonzero failure into a silent hook failure.

Concurrent session-start processes write the shared log with independent `O_TRUNC` descriptors and no serialization or atomic replacement. If two writers open before either writes, the later shorter write can leave a suffix from the other payload, producing invalid or misleading JSON instead of the documented last-pass result.

The detached command discards stderr and is never waited on. Any uv startup, import, or early Python failure before _write_store_log runs leaves no new log or SessionStart context; an old clean log may remain, so the required reconciliation silently disappears. Consequently aged reservations cannot write the mandatory DEFERRED-HIL/NOTIFY rows, while C-HE-20 explicitly requires the existing HITL queue and forbids a new escalation store. Only the gh_view call is protected; response-shape processing is not. A successful command returning valid JSON with a non-object shape makes .get raise AttributeError, which reconcile_all also does not catch, aborting the entire pass instead of failing safe per arc. Every persisted state other than terminal or pending falls through to the open branch. A semantically corrupt head such as state="bogus" with pr=null is reported as "open" with CLI rc 0, defeating the advertised corrupt-head isolation. Validate state against STATES before dispatch.

Searching the entire JSON log for the substring ERROR does not inspect the authoritative rc or result values. A successful result for a valid arc id containing ERROR, such as U-ERROR-1, produces a false resv=ERR warning despite rc=0. Parse the JSON and test its rc field.

The new sole-carrier family was not added to test_store_audit.py's FAMILY_RELATION and SOLE_FACTS pins. Reclassifying this row as derived or replacing its asserted authority fact still leaves the audit tests green, so the new one-authority claim is not actually verified.

This activates reconciliation even though loop_log_structured is absent at this HEAD. Every aged reservation therefore fails before writing the required DEFERRED-HIL/NOTIFY rows; reconcile_all merely records ERROR in .reconcile.log, so C-HE-20's durable HITL escalation is not performed. The added tests hide this by monkeypatching emit_loop_row. Land the writer with this caller or defer activation until it exists.

A malformed or unknown gh response sets state=None but then falls through to the aged open-stuck branch, emitting durable rows that falsely say the PR is still OPEN. This contradicts the stated treatment as a gh failure and can create spurious operator blocks. Return through the fail-safe path when state is unrecognized; the non-dict test currently checks only the returned state and misses the false emission.

The new single-arc reconcile CLI invokes reconcile outside reconcile_all's corruption guard, while main catches only ReservationError. A syntactically valid malformed head such as {} raises KeyError at head['lane_id'], producing an uncontrolled traceback and exit 1 instead of the CLI's fail-closed ABORT/exit-2 contract. At this HEAD, tools/hooks/loop_lib.sh has no loop_log_structured() definition, so this condition is always false: SessionStart neither surfaces .reconcile.log nor launches reconcile-all. The committed session-start reconciliation path is therefore entirely dormant, contrary to the U-HE-18 caller contract. Because the loop ledger retains a deferral until explicitly resolved, successfully reconciled reservations remain permanently pending in SessionStart summaries.

The detached reconciliation redirects both streams to /dev/null and its exit status is never observed. An import/launch failure or _write_store_log failure therefore leaves a missing or stale success log and produces no additionalContext error, so the unattended hook can silently fail.

The single-arc reconcile CLI supplies no on_unconfirmed callback. A gh timeout, command failure, malformed JSON, or unknown state is converted by reconcile() to "open", after which this command exits 0; automation therefore cannot distinguish confirmed OPEN ground truth from a reconciliation that never obtained ground truth.
